analysis: Both changed files are documentation only, with no code, config, or endpoint changes. docs/provider/direct-mode.md adds a section (head lines 176-210) on an experimental, default-absent NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP owner hook. The text says no production callsite installs it, and that it reuses the existing local auth, body limits, JSON/SSE framing and cancellation scope. It also describes concurrency 429s, 400s for contradictory controls, 422s for tool/schema violations, and image URI handling where content selects PNG or JPEG. The unchanged Authentication section (lines 96-112) still documents LocalAuthResponder as the outermost layer, with unauthenticated health routes only, and no TLS or rate limiting. The doc claims the hook inherits that auth, but the hook source (NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift) was not supplied, so that inheritance and the media/image-decode bounds are unverified. This is a coverage limit, not a finding. docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md only bumps the date and adds a note (head lines 13-15) that Nemotron Super VL has no qualified RAM tier or serving recommendation, which is conservative and does not alter the memory-gate claims. Relevant threats if the hook later ships: T-050, since inline image/video plaintext could reach temp files; T-041, for prefix-cache and KV retention; and T-010, since the doc says cancellation must retain media/KV ownership until native retirement. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by this PR. A later code PR that wires the hook should verify that auth ordering, body caps, image decode memory bounds, and no plaintext media on disk hold.
